arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Kroger stated the court of appeals applied Arizona v. Fulminante.
Wax argued Moore established prejudice from his lawyer's failure.
Sotomayor questioned the impact of a suppressible confession on plea reasonableness.
Ginsburg asked if removing the confession improves plea bargain outcomes.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Premo argues his plea was unreasonable because his lawyer ignored a coerced confession. Moore argues the plea remained reasonable despite the confession.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Premo wants the plea declared unreasonable due to the coerced confession.
Moore wants the plea upheld as reasonable despite the confession.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Premo claims his lawyer failed to recognize the confession was inadmissible.
Moore claims the plea remained reasonable even if the confession was suppressed.

paragraphs: Justice Sotomayor asked if a defendant should plead guilty with a suppressible confession.

paragraphs: This case defines how coerced confessions affect guilty plea validity. It sets the standard for evaluating plea reasonableness. It impacts how courts weigh inadmissible evidence in plea deals.
